garmin-half-2014.headline: My first half marathon.
memory: This was my first half marathon. Finishing under two hours was a big goal for me, and I was very proud of the accomplishment.
More than the course or any single moment, what stayed with me was the feeling that I had done something new and difficult and had done it well.

abes-amble-2014.headline: A fun 10K with my mom and Aunt Mary Kay.

milestone.label: Together
milestone.note: We ran the whole race together

memory: I ran Abe's Amble with my mom and Aunt Mary Kay, and the three of us stayed together for the whole 10K.
What I remember most is that it was simply a fun race through the Illinois State Fairgrounds. Running it together is what makes the day stand out.

photos.alt: Alex Ford with his mom and Aunt Mary Kay after the 2014 Abe's Amble 10K.
photos.caption: My mom, Aunt Mary Kay, and me after running Abe's Amble together.

pi-miler-2015.headline: My first day of trail racing started with a podium.
memory: This was my first day of trail running. The day started with the 3.14-mile race, and I surprised myself by finishing third.
That was only the beginning. After the 3.14-miler, I lined up for the Pi Day River Rotation Half Marathon and spent the rest of the day discovering how much I enjoyed trail racing.

pi-day-half-2015.headline: The half marathon that finished my first day of trail racing.
memory: The Pi Day River Rotation was my first day of trail running. I had already raced the 3.14-miler earlier that day and finished third.
Then I ran the half marathon. I really enjoyed it, and that enjoyment is what I remember most. It was a full day of trail racing and a great introduction to a different kind of running.

illinois-5k-2015.headline: A good shakeout before my first marathon.
memory: The Illinois 5K was a good shakeout race. The real goal that weekend was the next morning, when I would line up for my first marathon.
I wanted to get moving, enjoy the race weekend, and then be ready for 26.2 miles the next day.

illinois-marathon-2015.headline: My first marathon, finished in a thunderstorm.
memory: This was my first marathon, and I was already proud just to be out there taking on 26.2 miles.

Then a thunderstorm rolled in and it poured. Police were driving around the course telling runners to seek shelter. I was determined to finish, so I picked up the pace and kept going until I made it to the finish.
The weekend was special for my family too. My mom ran her first half marathon that weekend, so we both came away from Champaign with a first.

photos.alt: Alex Ford running the 2015 Illinois Marathon in heavy rain.
photos.caption: The rain coming down during my first marathon.

photos.alt: Alex Ford with his mom after the 2015 Illinois Marathon weekend.
photos.caption: My first marathon and my mom's first half marathon, on the same weekend.

heartland-39-3-2016.headline: Five weeks that showed me how well I could run.

milestone.label: Series
milestone.note: Three half marathons in five weeks

memory: I wanted something that would keep me training, so I signed up for the Heartland 39.3 Series.

I surprised myself with how well I ran Rock the Parkway, the first race in the series. That changed my expectations. Instead of just completing the series, I wanted to see if I could run even better in the races that followed.

One week later I set a half-marathon PR at Garmin in 1:43:16. During the same spring stretch I also raced the Illinois 5K and Half, setting a 21:02 5K race PR. I finished Heartland at Running With the Cows in 1:43:29.6, almost matching my half PR.
When the series was over, I was proud not only that I had finished it, but that I had been running so well and racing so often.

rock-parkway-half-2016.headline: The race that raised my expectations.
memory: I entered the Heartland 39.3 because I wanted something to keep me training.
At Rock the Parkway I surprised myself with how well I ran. That first result gave me confidence and motivated me to try to run even better in the races that followed.

garmin-half-2016.headline: A half-marathon PR one week later.
memory: One week after surprising myself at Rock the Parkway, I ran the Garmin Half and set my half-marathon PR at 1:43:16.
That PR is what stands out. The first Heartland race had made me want to see if I could improve, and at Garmin I did.

illinois-5k-2016.headline: My 5K race PR.
memory: This was part of the same spring stretch when I was racing constantly and running very well.
I ran 21:02 at the Illinois 5K, which became my official 5K race PR. The next morning I was back on the starting line for the Illinois Half Marathon.

illinois-half-2016.headline: A beautiful spring day in the Midwest.
memory: What I remember most about the Illinois Half is the day itself. It was a beautiful spring day in the Midwest.
I had run my 21:02 5K PR the night before, and the half was another race in a stretch where I was running and racing more often than I ever had.

running-with-cows-half-2016.headline: Finishing the Heartland 39.3 strong.
memory: Running With the Cows was the final race of the Heartland 39.3 Series.

I remember being proud when I finished. I had raced often, stayed consistent with my training, and run really well throughout the spring. Finishing the series in 1:43:29.6, almost matching my Garmin PR, was a great way to close it out.

big-ten-10k-2016.headline: A very fun race along Lake Michigan.
memory: I remember the Big Ten 10K as a very fun race along Lake Michigan.
There is not a bigger story I need to attach to it. Running along the lake in Chicago and enjoying the race is what stayed with me.

disney-princess-half-2018.headline: Running Abby's first half marathon with her.
memory: I ran the Disney Princess Half Marathon with Abby during the weekend I turned 30.
What matters most to me about the race is that it was Abby's first half marathon. Getting to run the whole experience with her is the memory I want to keep from that weekend.

photos.alt: Alex Ford and Abby after the 2018 Disney Princess Half Marathon.
photos.caption: Running Abby's first half marathon together during my 30th birthday weekend.
